notices.title: Protection against liens and civil action notice (owner steps to lien protection)
notices.cite: Utah Code 38-11-108; Utah Admin. Code R156-38a-108
notices.trigger: Every contract between an original contractor and a homeowner
notices.format: Notice in substantially the official form, prominently in an easy-to-read type style and size; the X. is the contract's own paragraph number; items (1) to (3) print together
notices.support: shall prominently appear in an easy-to-read type style and size in every contract between an original contractor and homeowner
notices.summary_row: The notice wording for every original contractor and homeowner contract
notices.block: Utah Admin. Code R156-38a-108. Notification of Rights under Title 38, Chapter 11
notices.hold_reason: The block opens with the rule heading and an instruction sentence, prints the contract paragraph number as "X.", and the $5,000 exemption cannot be decided by the builder; a person must prepare it.

notices.title: Direct solicitation sale cancellation notice (12 point dark bold, first page)
notices.trigger: Sale over $25 made other than at the supplier's established place of business after the supplier's personal contact (in person, mail, email, fax or telephone)
notices.format: Conspicuous statement in dark bold, at least 12-point type, on the first page of the purchase documentation; no separate state form
notices.support: be a conspicuous statement written in dark bold with at least 12-point type on the first page of the purchase documentation
notices.hold_reason: the block holds the notice wording together with a parenthetical instruction to the supplier that the file says is not words to print, and the exemption rule in subsection (3)(b), which should not print in the customer's contract

notices.title: Automatic renewal notice on the first page of the service contract
notices.trigger: Service, maintenance or repair contract on real property (recurring cleaning or pool service) with an automatic renewal period over 12 months
notices.format: Written notice, prominently displayed on the first page of the contract, in clear and understandable language and easy-to-read type
notices.support: a seller shall provide written notice of an automatic renewal provision prominently displayed on the first page of the service contract
notices.summary_row: Automatic renewal of service contracts on real property (cleaning, pool service)
notices.hold_reason: no prescribed wording; the statute only requires a written notice of the automatic renewal provision on the first page, and the block holds definitions and remedy rules around it

changes.new: Three business days after the later of the transaction or receipt of the product, for direct solicitation sales over $25 (Utah Code 13-11-4)
changes.support: AFTER THE DATE OF THE TRANSACTION OR RECEIPT OF THE PRODUCT, WHICHEVER IS LATER

changes.new: Sales over $25 made other than at the supplier's established place of business after the supplier's personal contact, whether in person, by mail, email, fax or telephone, on top of the federal rule; exempt if the supplier's own cancellation policy gives the buyer greater rights
changes.support: the sale is made other than at the supplier's established place of business pursuant to the supplier's personal contact, whether through mail, electronic mail, facsimile transmission, telephone, or any other form of direct solicitation

changes.new: Three business days counted from the later of the transaction date or receipt of the product; business day is not defined in the sections read.
changes.support: Day count: three business days after the later of the transaction date or receipt of the product; "business day" is not defined in the paragraphs read.

changes.new: DOPL license; work with a contracted or agreed value under $7,000 including labor and materials is exempt (over $3,000 needs a one-time insurance affirmation); electrical, plumbing, gas, fire, alarm, HVAC and radon stay licensed; insurance $1,000,000 and $2,000,000 for new applicants April 20, 2026
changes.support: Confirmed: "a contracted or agreed value of less than $7,000, including both labor and materials, and including all changes or additions"; over $3,000 the person files a one-time insurance affirmation with the division. Electrical, plumbing, gas, fire, alarm, HVAC and radon work stay licensed.

new.rule: Renewal that keeps the contract running past six months needs written notice 30 to 90 calendar days before the consumer's last day to cancel (personally, by certified mail, or on the first page of a monthly statement), plus first-page notice when the renewal period exceeds 12 months; otherwise the renewal clause is void and the contract goes month to month
new.scope_and_confidence: OFFICIAL text read at le.utah.gov. Applies to recurring cleaning and pool service.

changes.support: The Service Contracts Act applies to recurring cleaning and pool service
Utah has one that reaches cleaning and pool service: the Service Contracts Act, Utah Code 15-10
Utah has one that reaches cleaning and pool service: the Service Contracts Act, Utah Code 15-10

unsure: UT-lien: the official notice begins with the placeholder X. (the contract's own paragraph number), which will print as written because the builder cannot number it, and the block opens with a one-sentence instruction line naming where the notice goes.

UT-lien: the rule says the notice is for contracts between an original contractor and a homeowner; the residential key is the closest thing the builder can tell, and the file does not say whether jobs under $5,000 are exempt from printing it.

UT-cancel: the notice belongs in the contract, but the block mixes the wording with a supplier-instruction parenthetical and the exemption rule, so it is held; the rule also reaches phone, mail and email sales, which sold_in_home does not capture.
UT-auto-renew: added; the notice is only required when a renewal period exceeds 12 months, which the builder cannot tell, and no wording is prescribed.

cleaning.home_solicitation_applies_to_cleaning: left false, but 13-11-4(2)(m) reaches any sale away from the supplier's place of business, so a cleaning plan sold at the home may be covered; the file does not say so outright.
